Diego (Design): Quick UX review — thinking about the model catalog legend, the performance badges, and the pin-to-compare behaviour. Observations: legend wording is vague (people interpret 'performance' differently), badges are visually noisy, and currently pinning a version in the UI doesn't make it obvious which variant is being compared. Thoughts? Ava (PM): +1 on the ambiguity. Users asked what 'performance' actually means. Suggest we separate labels into explicit axes (latency / throughput / cost) or adopt a small taxonomy (Fast / Balanced / High-quality) with numeric hover detail. Sam (Frontend): Also seeing contrast issues with the current badge colors when shown over table rows — keyboard focus ring is subtle. We should avoid relying on color alone for state, and ensure 3:1 contrast for the badge background vs text at least. Marta (A11y): Agree. Also we need accessible tooltip behavior for badges: tooltip must be reachable by keyboard and exposed to screen readers. Consider `role="tooltip"` + `aria-describedby` on the badge; for pin/focus changes use `aria-live="polite"` announcements. Example: ```
Fast
p50=32ms · p95=120ms · est $0.002/token
``` Priya (Eng-ML): Related implementation note: pinning a version currently only updates the UI state; for correctness we should persist a pinned_variant_id server-side and return it in the catalog API so clients display the exact model-variant being compared. Proposed API change: POST /catalog/models/:id/pin -> { pinned_variant_id: "v2-quant" } (backwards-compatible if we keep old response fields). Diego (Design): For the legend copy, what about renaming the legend header to "Performance profile" and adding short inline microcopy: "Latency · Cost · Quality — hover a badge for details". If space is tight show icons and collapse labels into a hover panel. Ava (PM): Prefer "Performance profile" wording. Also suggest changing the pin CTA text from "Lock" to "Pin version to compare" — earlier tests showed "Lock" confused non-technical users. Sam (Frontend): I can prototype a compact legend with icons + stacked tooltip for hover/focus. Will create keyboard-only states (focus-visible) and test color-blind palettes. ETA: prototype in Figma in 48h, dev PR within a week. OpsBot: Staging preview deployed: https://staging.redwood.ai/catalog?legend=v2 — use ?legend=v2 for the compact legend and badge tooltips. Marta (A11y): Also recommend a skip link at the top of the catalog: "Skip to compare table" for quick keyboard navigation, and ensure pinned changes are announced: `aria-live` message like "Pinned model version v2-quant for comparison." Priya (Eng-ML): On server side I'll draft the minimal API contract doc. Note: pinning should also preserve effective KV cache hints for dedicated/private deployments — we may need a migration to record cache hints per pinned_variant. Will outline implications for rollout. Diego (Design): One more UX nit: when you pin a version in a compare row, we should visually surface the reason (e.g., "Pinned by user — will remain until unpinned") and show a small undo toast. Ava (PM): Let's run this as a behind-feature-flag canary and A/B test whether the compact legend reduces support tickets. Proposal: 2-week experiment after rollout. Sam (Frontend): Sounds good. I'll include telemetry hooks (legendOpened, badgeHovered, pinToggled) in the prototype so we can measure clicks and hover rates. Priya (Eng-ML): I need the spec before changing the API; I'll wait for Diego/Ava final copy and the product ticket. I'll also list edge-cases for Dedicated/Private customers. Diego (Design): Thanks — I'll consolidate notes and drop a design mock link in this thread tomorrow. If anyone has examples of confusing copy from user transcripts, please paste them here. Ava (PM): I'll open the product ticket and include acceptance criteria (accessible tooltip, persisted pinned_variant_id, legend microcopy, telemetry). Marta (A11y): Quick reminder: include keyboard-only screenshots in the ticket to avoid surprises in QA. Sam (Frontend): Will do. :+1: Priya (Eng-ML): On it. Diego (Design): Awesome — thanks team, follow-up thread will have mocks and API sketch.
